Subject: Edgeretail discovery recap: inference unit economics & next steps

Hi Alex / Tara —

Thanks for the conversation earlier. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned and can move to a technical deep-dive: 

Pain points you shared
- Inference cost during promotions spikes (token volume + concurrency) is the single-largest margin drag.
- Current endpoints are running on single-tenant SageMaker instances; you don’t have an efficient batching or KV/prefix cache layer, so per-token cost is high.
- SLOs: marketing pages need ~p95 < 350ms for single-shot scoring; critical checkout flows need ~100 QPS sustained for specific routes.

Current stack notes you gave
- Models hosted on SageMaker (p3 -> occasionally scaled to p4).
- No quantization in production today.
- Rudimentary autoscaling; long tail of cold starts during promos.

Success criteria (what would make this a win)
- Unit economics: move to <$0.0008 per token on average for high-volume routes (pilot target).
- Maintain p95 latency <350ms for single-shot scoring in prod.
- Achieve 20–40% cost reduction via batching/caching/quantization without ≥10% quality regression.

What Redwood can do (high level)
- Continuous batching + smart routing to keep latency while increasing throughput.
- KV / prefix caching for common prompt prefixes (marketing templates), typically 15–40% token savings on eligible traffic.
- Quantization options (int8/int4) with quality-guard rails and A/B evals.
- Dedicated pilot with telemetry (token-level cost, p95/p99 latency, quality regressions).

Next steps (agreed)
1) I’m attaching a quick cost estimate for a 6-week pilot (redwood-quick-estimate.xlsx).
2) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with your infra/ML infra team next week — suggested slots Tue/Wed mornings.
3) Share basic environment and compliance asks (I’ll loop in security) — see attached environment-asklist.txt.
4) Marissa will send a short SOW draft and proposed pilot commitment.

Attachments: redwood-quick-estimate.xlsx, environment-asklist.txt
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345678

Thanks — I’ll follow up with proposed times in a separate calendar invite.

— Sergio

Thanks, Sergio — solid summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side so you can tailor the deep dive: 

- Quantization: we are open to int8 and int4 experiments as long as we can run side-by-side quality checks. Our models are a mix of fine-tuned open weights and some propriety layers — we’ll need to confirm compatibility but are generally open.
- Caching: when you say 'prefix caching' — does that imply token-level KV reuse across requests or more of a template result cache? For marketing pages we expect many near-identical prompts (only product_id changes).
- Pilot throughput: for the pilot, we can commit to a 50 QPS sustained test window for two separate routes. Is that sufficient to validate cost curves?

Happy to join the deep-dive. Tue AM works for our ML infra lead. I’ll also loop in our SRE (Tara) for any infra specifics.

Appreciate the quick estimate attachment — will review and get back with internal notes.

— Alex

Subject: Re: Edgeretail discovery recap: inference unit economics & next steps

Alex — quick answers inline and a proposed plan: 

- Quantization: we’ll run int8 and int4 experiments in a canary lane. Our Optimize toolkit computes expected token-quality curves; if you give us a small eval set we’ll return expected ROUGE/Perplexity deltas and suggested thresholds.
- Prefix caching: this is token-level KV reuse inside the runtime for identical prefixes + a lightweight template cache for identical prompts. In practice marketing templates where only product_id changes are excellent candidates for prefix caching — we typically see 25–35% token savings on those patterns.
- Pilot sizing: 50 QPS sustained for two routes is a good validation window to estimate cost curves. For reliability checks we’ll also run a 10-minute spike to 150 QPS to validate autoscaling + cold-start behavior.

Proposed timeline:
- Thu: send SOW draft + scoped pilot definition (6 weeks) — attached discovery-notes-edgeretail.pdf with the scope highlights.
- Tue (deep-dive): Tech session with ML infra + SRE to walk integration points, auth, and data flows.
- Post-pilot: produce a regression report and final unit economics analysis to inform a Dedicated capacity recommendation.

I’ve attached a short discovery notes PDF and the quick estimate spreadsheet (redwood-quick-estimate.xlsx).

Best,
